_**User (1970-01-01 00:00:00Z)**_

I have a p5js sketch with a main canvas, and additional pgraphics objects that are visible in the page. How can I check if the mouse is over one of the pGraphics objects?

---

_**Agent**_

To check if the mouse is over one of the `pGraphics` objects in a p5.js sketch, you can compare the mouse coordinates with the position and dimensions of the `pGraphics` objects. Here's a step-by-step plan:

1. Define the position and dimensions of each `pGraphics` object.
2. Create a function to check if the mouse is within the bounds of a `pGraphics` object.
3. Use this function in the `draw` or `mouseMoved` function to check if the mouse is over any `pGraphics` object.

Here's an example implementation:

```javascript
let pg1, pg2;
let pg1X = 50, pg1Y = 50, pg1Width = 200, pg1Height = 200;
let pg2X = 300, pg2Y = 50, pg2Width = 200, pg2Height = 200;

function setup() {
  createCanvas(600, 400);
  pg1 = createGraphics(pg1Width, pg1Height);
  pg2 = createGraphics(pg2Width, pg2Height);
}

function draw() {
  background(220);

  // Draw pGraphics objects
  pg1.background(100);
  pg2.background(150);
  image(pg1, pg1X, pg1Y);
  image(pg2, pg2X, pg2Y);

  // Check if mouse is over any pGraphics object
  if (isMouseOver(pg1X, pg1Y, pg1Width, pg1Height)) {
    fill(255, 0, 0);
    text('Mouse over pg1', 10, height - 20);
  } else if (isMouseOver(pg2X, pg2Y, pg2Width, pg2Height)) {
    fill(255, 0, 0);
    text('Mouse over pg2', 10, height - 20);
  } else {
    fill(0);
    text('Mouse not over any pGraphics', 10, height - 20);
  }
}

function isMouseOver(x, y, w, h) {
  return mouseX > x && mouseX < x + w && mouseY > y && mouseY < y + h;
}
```

In this example:
- `pg1` and `pg2` are `pGraphics` objects.
- `pg1X`, `pg1Y`, `pg1Width`, `pg1Height` define the position and dimensions of `pg1`.
- `pg2X`, `pg2Y`, `pg2Width`, `pg2Height` define the position and dimensions of `pg2`.
- The `isMouseOver` function checks if the mouse is within the bounds of a given `pGraphics` object.
- The `draw` function uses `isMouseOver` to display a message indicating whether the mouse is over any `pGraphics` object.

_**User (1970-01-01 00:00:00Z)**_

That doesn't line up with how my sketch works - the 2 graphics objects are displayed on the page, but not within the main canvas object. How would a vanilla-js script check for mouse-over events on a given object?

---

_**Agent**_

To check for mouse-over events on a given HTML element using vanilla JavaScript, you can use event listeners. Here's a step-by-step plan:

1. Select the HTML elements you want to check for mouse-over events.
2. Add event listeners for `mouseover` and `mouseout` events to these elements.
3. Define the event handler functions to handle the mouse-over and mouse-out events.

Here's an example implementation:

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>Mouse Over Example</title>
  <style>
    .graphics {
      width: 200px;
      height: 200px;
      margin: 20px;
      display: inline-block;
    }
    #pg1 {
      background-color: lightblue;
    }
    #pg2 {
      background-color: lightgreen;
    }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <div id="pg1" class="graphics"></div>
  <div id="pg2" class="graphics"></div>
  <p id="status">Mouse not over any graphics</p>

  <script>
    const pg1 = document.getElementById('pg1');
    const pg2 = document.getElementById('pg2');
    const status = document.getElementById('status');

    pg1.addEventListener('mouseover', () => {
      status.textContent = 'Mouse over pg1';
    });

    pg1.addEventListener('mouseout', () => {
      status.textContent = 'Mouse not over any graphics';
    });

    pg2.addEventListener('mouseover', () => {
      status.textContent = 'Mouse over pg2';
    });

    pg2.addEventListener('mouseout', () => {
      status.textContent = 'Mouse not over any graphics';
    });
  </script>
</body>
</html>
```

In this example:
- Two `div` elements with IDs `pg1` and `pg2` represent the graphics objects.
- The `mouseover` event listener changes the text content of the `status` paragraph to indicate which element the mouse is over.
- The `mouseout` event listener resets the text content of the `status` paragraph when the mouse leaves the element.
